title: Polity and Administrative Structure of Assam

blocks.content: Covers Assam's state governance framework, autonomous councils, and the specific constitutional provisions relevant to the Northeast — a distinctive, high-value area given Assam's unique administrative arrangements under the Sixth Schedule.

items: Assam has a unicameral state legislature — the Assam Legislative Assembly, located in Dispur; the state does not have a Legislative Council (upper house).

The Governor of Assam is the constitutional/nominal head of state, appointed by the President of India; the Chief Minister, who leads the party/coalition with a majority in the Legislative Assembly, is the head of government and exercises actual executive authority.
The state is represented in the Parliament of India through seats in both the Lok Sabha (directly elected) and the Rajya Sabha (elected by the Legislative Assembly).

The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the administration of certain tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram through Autonomous District Councils, granting them a degree of legislative, executive, and judicial autonomy over local matters.

In Assam, key autonomous councils established under or alongside this framework include the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council, the North Cachar Hills (Dima Hasao) Autonomous Council, and the Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC/BTR) — each granting varying degrees of self-governance to the respective communities/regions.

The Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR) — created following the Bodo Accord, most recently updated in 2020 — governs Bodo-majority areas of Assam through the Bodoland Territorial Council, with its own elected council and defined administrative powers.

These autonomous arrangements are a distinctive feature of Assam's administrative structure, reflecting the state's ethnic and linguistic diversity, and are frequently tested given their constitutional and current-affairs relevance.

Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) — a three-tier system (Gram Panchayat, Anchalik Panchayat/Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad) operates in the rural, non-Sixth-Schedule areas of Assam, following the general pattern established under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.

Urban local bodies — Municipal Corporations (e.g., Guwahati Municipal Corporation), Municipal Boards, and Town Committees govern urban areas, following the pattern established under the 74th Constitutional Amendment.
Areas under the Sixth Schedule autonomous councils generally have a distinct local governance structure (through the councils themselves) rather than the standard Panchayati Raj system.

The Gauhati High Court, located in Guwahati, is the High Court with jurisdiction over Assam and, historically/functionally, several other Northeastern states (with some now having their own dedicated benches/High Courts).

The Assam Public Service Commission (APSC) is the state's constitutional body responsible for conducting recruitment examinations for various state civil service and other posts, functioning analogously to the UPSC at the central level.

Key state government initiatives and departments periodically feature in current-affairs-linked GS questions, so staying updated on recent institutional developments is valuable ahead of any specific exam cycle.

cells:
Exam Tip

• The Sixth Schedule and its Autonomous District Councils (Karbi Anglong, Dima Hasao/N.C. Hills, Bodoland) are among the most distinctively 'Assam-specific' and therefore most frequently tested polity topics — prioritize this over generic Indian Polity content already covered elsewhere.

• The distinction between Sixth Schedule autonomous council areas and standard Panchayati Raj areas is a frequently tested conceptual question.

• Assam Legislative Assembly being unicameral (no Legislative Council) is a simple but consistently tested direct-recall fact.

Q2. The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution primarily provides for the administration of:
B. Certain tribal areas through Autonomous District Councils
Answer: Certain tribal areas through Autonomous District Councils
Q3. The Bodoland Territorial Council governs which region of Assam?
B. Bodo-majority areas under the Bodoland Territorial Region
Answer: Bodo-majority areas under the Bodoland Territorial Region
